Death Knight Blood Rotation in 

 

 

 
 Manage buffs and debuffs 
From being rewarded with bonus armor and Runic Power cost reduction from Bone Shield to Hemostasis to amplify your self-healing, these simple buffs are core to your rotation. You don't need to go out of your way for them, either! 

 

 

 
 Keep cooldowns on cooldown 
 Dancing Rune Weapon and all your defensive cooldowns are the bread and butter of the spec! 

 

 

 
 Optimize resources 
The rest of the spec revolves around spending Runes to convert them into Runic Power as efficiently as possible. More Runic Power = more Death Strike ! 
 

If you're looking for a more bite-sized explanation, check out our starter guide below:

Blood Death Knight Starter Guide

 Best Death Knight Blood Single Target Rotation

 Blood Death Knight's single target rotation operates on a priority list, maintaining two crucial buffs and using resources to optimize Runic Power generation. Every GCD depends on the current state of resources and active abilities at your disposal. As a result, this section should be read as a priority list, and not a strict sequence.

 Please select a Hero Talent option to generate a Single Target priority 

 The builds used below are covered in the Talents page. Anywhere you see the icon, you can hover over it for additional notes. 

 Deathbringer puts a strong emphasis on its signature ability, Reaper's Mark , and the subsequent procs and effects it generates when it expires. The rotational gameplay is otherwise the same, with a much smaller focus on the management of Bone Shield thanks to the charges Reaper's Mark indirectly provides.
 
Priority

 
Cast Death Strike if you need the healing or are above 75 Runic PowerWhy 75?
This is an arbitrary breakpoint that is a measured amount. It attempts to solve two problems:
 
With it at around this value, you always have two Death Strike available to you

You also need 45 RP - two to three full Heart Strike - to overcap Runic Power

Maintain at least 5 charges of Bone Shield . If Bone Shield is about to expire, press Marrowrend Are there other generators?
As , every 45 seconds, you will predictably gain two Exterminate charges, guaranteeing a Bone Shield duration refresh and additional charges. On top of this, if you play Echoing Fury , you are also guaranteed to come out of Dancing Rune Weapon at essentially Bone Shield cap.

The problem with this is that, depending on how early you spend those Exterminate , you may need to add one Bone Shield generator at the halfway point between Dancing Rune Weapon .

If you are already on 8+ bones and do not have a problem in taunting a target, Death Grip works as an effective Bone Shield refresh.

Cast Death and Decay and stand in it if you are not currently affected by the buff it provides.

Cast Reaper's Mark on cooldown

Cast Dancing Rune Weapon on cooldown

Cast Blood Boil if Dancing Rune Weapon is active and your target does not have Blood Plague on it, or if you are about to cap on its charges

Cast Blood Boil if you have a Boiling Point proc

Cast Blood Boil as a filler if you have a charge of it available

Cast Heart Strike as a filler. Do not run out of runes, particularly around the 45-second mark when Reaper's Mark is about to come off cooldown

 San'layn greatly empowers Dancing Rune Weapon while also forcing the player in a feat-or-famine cycle around Essence of the Blood Queen , a buff that can easily be stacked and refreshed during Dancing Rune Weapon . Outside of this window of strength, this buff can only be refreshed as an infrequent proc on Death Strike - and a player needs to generate at least one proc every 20 seconds for up to 75 seconds to keep the stacks rolling, in order not to have to spend their entire time re-stacking it during the next Dancing Rune Weapon . A slightly stronger emphasis is put around fully empowering Consumption if you play it, and the penalty for mismanaging Death and Decay is stricter, but the broad priority outside of this remains the same: waste no resources and use cooldowns broadly on cooldown.

 Best Death Knight Blood Opener

Your opener as a Blood Death Knight depends on your Hero Talent choice. In both cases, your goal is to set up as many maintenance buffs as you can before the fight starts to cut down on wasteful GCDs you would spend doing so otherwise.

In the following section, we will assume that you are in control of pulling and can spend two global cooldowns preparing things.

 Please select a Hero Talent option to generate an Opener sequence 

 The builds used below are covered in the Talents page. Anywhere you see the icon, you can hover over it for additional notes. 

 Deathbringer 's opener sets up three elements as quickly as possible: it primes Death and Decay and Bone Shield , and makes sure to prioritize Reaper's Mark ahead of Dancing Rune Weapon . As the two always come back off cooldown roughly simultaneously if you do not desync them, this guarantees that this order will be preserved during the entire fight.

While Death's Caress is in flight, pre-place Death and Decay 

Cast Reaper's Mark 

Cast Dancing Rune Weapon 

Cast Blood Boil 

Cast Death Strike 

Proceed with normal priority

AoE Sequence

 
Gather the enemies or packs you intend to pull. You can weave Blood Boil , Heart Strike and Death Strike while doing so to build AoE threat

Near the end of your gather, pre-place Death and Decay where you intend to fight

Cast Reaper's Mark 

Cast Dancing Rune Weapon 

Cast Blood Boil 

Cast Death Strike 

Proceed with normal priority

 San'layn 's opener sets up all elements of resources as quickly as possible: it primes a Blood Plague plague ahead of Dancing Rune Weapon so that the first Blood Boil in it pandemics it to maximum duration, puts up Bone Shield ahead of everything else, primes Death and Decay and unleashes Dancing Rune Weapon to truly kick-start the Hero Talent's window of power with as few dead GCDs in it as possible.

Pre-Combat Check

Whilst Blood has no strict pre-combat checklist of group buffs and personal temporary buffs, there are still a couple of valuable resources you can prepare before a fight starts. We have detailed them below:

Raid

 Check Consumables - Flask, food, augment rune, temporary weapon oils or whetstones are worth having at all times.
 

Mythic+

 Blood Death Knight Major Cooldowns

Blood has access to a single offensive cooldown outside of its Hero Talent trees in Midnight, in the form of Dancing Rune Weapon . In addition to this, a number of defensive cooldowns are available, all with differing impact and niches. We have covered how they work, including all of the intricacies and niche use cases they may have below.

 Dancing Rune Weapon

 Dancing Rune Weapon grants you 20% parry for 12 seconds when cast, replicates a small subset of abilities ( Heart Strike , Marrowrend , Blood Boil and Death Strike ) and has two additional effects:
 
If you cast Marrowrend while it is active, you get 3 bonus Bone Shield for each Dancing Rune Weapon active

If you cast Blood Boil while it is active, each Dancing Rune Weapon applies its own copy of Blood Plague 
 

You can empower this spell through other talents, granting you 5% bonus parry for the first 8 seconds of it, and up to 10 Runic Power per second for the first 8 seconds. takes this up a notch by using this as their main activator for all Hero Talent mechanics.

 Death Knight Blood Advanced Tips

 
 Bone Shield Management 

The largest remaining optimization around Blood's toolkit and rotation involves familiarizing yourself with Bone Shield generators. Every 30 seconds, you will have to use one of them to refresh bones.

As , when playing Reaper's Onslaught , this is effectively dealt with for you. When playing Dark Talons , you can choose to delay one Exterminate explosion by ~5 seconds to fix this; alternatively, you can slot in a Death Grip to refresh your entire stack.

 Bone Shield management is significantly harder as , due to the hero talent not having any passive generation tools. You are left to your own devices - and to make things even worse, Apex talents have effectively randomized how many Bone Shield charges a single Marrowrend provides, since each Apex Dancing Rune Weapon provides its own bonus three stacks. Proper UI tracking goes a long way towards solving this, but there is still an element of skill involved.
